title: Federal health grant audits found late decisions, missing identifiers and a missed review

beats.text: Federal grant oversight goes beyond checking how much a grantee spends.

visual.sub: Two management decisions were issued after the required deadline

beats.text: In fiscal 2009 auditors tested 38 subrecipients across three programs.

visual.kicker: Two management decisions were issued after the required deadline

beats.text: Public Health missed a six-month deadline for two decisions on audit findings.
In the next audit, a different problem appeared in immunization grants.

visual.kicker: Immunization grantees received federal award notice late

beats.text: Recipients learned of federal funding during review, after the required initial notice.

visual.kicker: Immunization grantees received federal award notice late

beats.text: In fiscal 2012 some HIV grants lacked required organization identifiers before award.

visual.kicker: HIV grant reviews lacked identifiers and one required monitoring check

beats.text: The department told contractors to submit their identifiers.

visual.kicker: HIV grant reviews lacked identifiers and one required monitoring check

beats.text: Required monitoring was also missing for one of nine recipients tested.
The independent auditor returned the next year to check the changes.

visual.kicker: Auditors returned to test the FY2012 corrective action

beats.text: It verified that Public Health implemented the HIV program corrective action.

visual.kicker: Auditors returned to test the FY2012 corrective action

beats.text: The records identify different oversight failures. They do not establish a financial loss.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
